site.name: github-404
site.summary: github-404-clone Clone of the GitHub 404 error page. Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | 404 page: top GitHub nav bar, centered error message ("This is not the web page you are looking for."), Octocat illustration, links to home / search / contact support | | `style.css` | Dark background, illustration styling, buttons | | `app.js` | Illustration hover / parallax effect, (optional) fake search suggestions |

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full github-404 system, prioritizing the primary error page flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The GitHub-404 recovery experience generally works: the primary Search flow and the Contact Support submission can reach clear success states (e.g., “1 result for react” and “Submitted… within 24 hours”). However, several mobile and accessibility issues undermine confidence and usability, including an unlabeled, no-op-feeling header icon and multiple controls with small tap targets. FAQ and Status incident interactions often fail to provide reliable, obvious feedback (silent no-ops or unclear toggling), creating friction in secondary recovery paths.

exploration_plan.goal: Critique the UX of the github-404 clone by validating the primary 404 recovery flow (navigation + search + support/status links) and adjacent interactions (header nav, CTAs, interactive illustration behavior) on both desktop and mobile viewports.
exploration_plan.summary: Run an exploration centered on the single known page (index.html), focusing first on the recovery actions: header navigation (Search/Support/Status), the main “Search GitHub” input + Search button, and the “contact support” / “GitHub Status” links. Then validate interactive/visual elements driven by app.js (illustration hover/parallax and any fake search suggestions) and confirm keyboard focus, label accessibility, and tap-target sizing issues flagged in the prescan. Repeat the critical interactions on mobile viewport with attention to small/tappable header controls and the header layout.
assumptions: Only index.html is available in the prescan (single-page site); other “pages” are expected to be external or hash/navigation targets rather than local HTML files.
app.js adds hover/parallax behavior to the illustration and may implement optional fake search suggestions upon input/focus/typing.
The header controls (Search/Support/Status) and the main search likely route to external GitHub pages or anchors, but at minimum should change the UI state (submit/search handling) without crashes.
risk_hotspots: Header icon link labeled as empty (ux-1: clickable a '#', empty/unclear label) and small tap target size (32x32px) — accessibility and mobile usability risk.
Header nav links/button-like items (ux-2/ux-3/ux-4) have small tap targets (61x25px, 68x25px, 57x25px) — mobile hit-target risk.
Main search input (typeable: 'Search GitHub') and Search button (ux-6) behavior — confirm form submission, keyboard interaction, and any suggestion dropdown from app.js.
Secondary CTAs: 'contact support' (ux-10) and 'GitHub Status' (ux-11) are visually small (17px height text area) — tap target and readability risk on mobile.
Interactive illustration (Octocat/space scene) driven by app.js — validate it does not obstruct controls, remains performant, and works with hover vs touch (no hover on mobile).

phases.title: Baseline load + content comprehension (desktop)
phases.objective: Verify the 404 message, primary recovery options, and overall page usability on desktop without interaction.
key_checks: Confirm the main 404 headline and the guidance text are visible and readable at desktop viewport.
Check top navigation presence: Search, Support, Status, plus the left icon link.
Ensure the main input labeled/placeholder 'Search GitHub' is visible and not overlapped by illustration effects.
Tab through focus order from header to main search to links; confirm a visible focus indicator for interactive elements.
exit_criteria: User can understand this is a 404 page and see all key recovery actions (search, code/repositories/people options, contact support, GitHub Status).
No focus traps; tab order reaches all interactive controls without layout breaking.

phases.title: Primary recovery: Search input + submit behavior (desktop)
phases.objective: Validate the main search flow and any dynamic UI state (fake suggestions, button enablement, submission handling).
key_checks: Click into the 'Search GitHub' input and type a short query (e.g., 'react' or 'ux'); verify input responsiveness.
Press Enter and click the green 'Search' button; confirm no console errors and verify whether a results page opens or a simulated suggestion appears.
If app.js provides fake suggestions, verify they appear on input/focus and can be selected/clicked; otherwise verify absence is graceful.
Click Code, Repositories, and People controls beneath the search; confirm they change the selected mode/state or affect search parameters.
exit_criteria: Search interaction completes without errors (no blank UI/crashes).
Search mode buttons (Code/Repositories/People) show a clear state change (visual or behavioral) consistent with expectations.

phases.title: Adjacent recovery: Header nav + support/status links (desktop)
phases.objective: Validate secondary navigation actions for recovery and verify they are reachable, correctly labeled, and usable.
key_checks: Click header links: Search, Support, Status; verify navigation occurs or appropriate UI state changes without breaking layout.
Click 'contact support' and 'GitHub Status' links; confirm they respond (navigation or simulated behavior).
Re-check the small/empty-labeled icon link ('#') for usability: does it do anything meaningful, and is it keyboard accessible despite empty label.
Confirm external link styling/affordances are consistent (visited/unvisited not confusing).
exit_criteria: All header/support/status CTAs respond to click and do not produce broken states.
The unlabeled/empty-label control is still operable by keyboard; if it does nothing, the UX implications are observed.

phases.title: Illustration interactivity + performance safeguards (desktop)
phases.objective: Validate the app.js-driven hover/parallax behavior and ensure it does not interfere with the primary recovery controls.
key_checks: Hover over the Octocat/illustration area; verify parallax/hover effect triggers and does not cause visual jank.
Ensure the animation does not block pointer events or obscure the search input/button or links.
Scroll (if possible) and observe whether background/illustration movement causes layout shift near the input area (even though it’s an error page).
Check that interaction remains smooth; confirm no console errors during hover/animation.
exit_criteria: Illustration effects work as intended on hover and do not hinder access to search/support actions.
No console errors appear during interactive testing.

phases.title: Mobile critical path: tap usability + responsive layout (mobile)
phases.objective: Repeat the critical recovery interactions on mobile viewport, emphasizing small tap targets and touch behavior for illustration effects.
key_checks: Verify responsive layout: header items remain visible and not overlapping the search content.
Tap the empty-labeled icon link; confirm it is reachable and doesn’t frustrate (and observe any mis-tap due to small target).
Tap into 'Search GitHub' input, type a query, and submit via the Search button.
Tap Code/Repositories/People controls; confirm state change is discoverable on touch.
Tap 'contact support' and 'GitHub Status' and confirm they are hit reliably (no near-misses).
Touch/drag on the illustration area; verify there is no dead/unresponsive region that blocks scrolling/tapping controls.
exit_criteria: Mobile users can complete the full recovery path: focus search -> submit -> access support/status without mis-taps or layout breakage.
Touch behavior is consistent (no reliance on hover for critical functions).

coverage_targets.pages: visit all known HTML pages (100%: index.html)
coverage_targets.features: exercise all visible controls per prescan: header icon + Search/Support/Status, main search input + Search button, Code/Repositories/People, contact support, GitHub Status; validate illustration hover/parallax behavior at least once
coverage_targets.mobile: repeat phases 2-3 interactions (search + mode buttons + support/status + header links) on mobile viewport; additionally test illustration touch/gesture non-interference

notes: Limit scope to the single known local page (index.html). If header/search CTAs navigate externally, record destination changes and stop further deep exploration beyond the external destination (since no additional local pages are prescanned).
Prioritize accessibility/tap-target issues flagged in prescan (empty label for ux-1 and small tap targets) as they can materially affect UX on mobile.

findings.user_goal: Navigate using the header icon and understand what it will do
findings.problem: The top-left header icon is an interactive link but has no visible or accessible label, and it frequently behaves like a no-op (no navigation or meaningful state change).
findings.evidence: Tool notes: "Clicking the small unlabeled header icon (target_id ux-1, anchor with href="#") produced no observable navigation or visual/URL change (before_url==after_url)" and later also "Tapping the small header icon target... resulted in visible content change without navigation/URL change". Accessibility warnings: empty interactive label for ux-1; bbox 32x32 with small tap target warning.
findings.why_it_matters: Users may repeatedly tap a control they can’t interpret, reducing trust and increasing time-to-recovery—especially on mobile where the hit target is small.
findings.suggestion: Add a visible label and/or accessible name (aria-label/title), increase the tap target to at least 44px, and ensure tapping produces a clear and consistent outcome (navigation or an obvious state change). If it’s decorative, make it non-interactive.
findings.source_hint: mobile top-left header icon: dom_summary interactable ux-1; layout_warning_count includes empty_interactive_label and small_tap_target

findings.user_goal: Use Status incident history to view details or understand system updates
findings.problem: Incident history row taps often result in silent no-ops with no obvious highlight/expansion or navigation feedback.
findings.evidence: Multiple steps report taps without change: e.g., “Clicking the incident row ... did not produce an obvious UX change: tool_result reports no visible-text/URL change” and later “Tapping the incident row... produced no detectable visual or navigational change (changed=false)”. Scroll also did not move viewport (y unchanged). One row showed expansion (“Webhook delivery delays” had detail text), suggesting behavior is inconsistent across rows.
findings.why_it_matters: When taps appear to do nothing, users can’t rely on Status as a recovery channel, and may miss important incident details.
findings.suggestion: Make row selection feedback explicit on mobile (highlight selected row, chevron rotation, expand/collapse animation, and ensure tapped row reliably reveals details). If some rows are non-expandable, label them accordingly and provide an affordance difference.
findings.source_hint: Status view incident rows: targets ux-67, ux-52; recent_chunks steps 19-30 and 55-61

findings.user_goal: Use FAQ accordion to quickly find help topics
findings.problem: FAQ accordion interaction is inconsistent and often fails to provide clear visible feedback/toggling after taps.
findings.evidence: On mobile: "Tapping the FAQ question ... produced no obvious response/visibility change" and screenshots show answers not expanded for certain questions (e.g., “How do I set up a custom domain…” and “What are GitHub Actions?”). In other cases, answers appear expanded despite tool saying changed=false (indicating inconsistent wiring or detection).
findings.why_it_matters: Users depend on FAQ toggles for fast self-service; unclear or unreliable accordion behavior increases frustration and time-to-resolution.
findings.suggestion: Ensure each tap deterministically toggles the matching panel and updates visual indicators (chevron state and smooth expansion). Provide immediate visual feedback (e.g., loading shimmer if async).
findings.source_hint: FAQ accordion items: steps 49-67 and 73-78; mobile screenshots show chevrons/expanded text inconsistently

findings.user_goal: Switch between recovery sections (Search/Support/Status) and operate them reliably on mobile
findings.problem: Primary navigation controls have small tap targets and can be hard to hit accurately on mobile.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings show “Search” 61x25px, “Support” 69x25px, “Status” 57x25px, all below the 44px guidance; multiple small tap target warnings on mobile header items (ux-2/ux-3/ux-4).
findings.why_it_matters: Small targets increase mis-taps, especially on error pages where users are already stressed and moving quickly.
findings.suggestion: Increase tap target height to meet mobile guidance, add spacing between nav items, and consider a sticky bottom nav or larger tab buttons for mobile.
findings.source_hint: mobile header nav: dom_summary layout_warning_count small_tap_target for ux-2/ux-3/ux-4

findings.user_goal: Recover by contacting support with clear, field-level guidance
findings.problem: Form validation feedback appears primarily generic (“Please fill all fields”) rather than clearly tied to specific missing fields, making error recovery harder.
findings.evidence: Tool notes: after Submit Request, validation shows “Please fill all fields” and "error message itself is not clearly tied to specific required fields (Email/Subject/Description)". On mobile, objective notes also indicate limited validation clarity (only general message).
findings.why_it_matters: Generic error messages force users to guess what’s wrong, increasing abandonment on a recovery-critical flow.
findings.suggestion: Provide inline, field-level errors (e.g., highlight Email/Description/Subject) and announce which fields are missing, plus keep focus on the first invalid field.
findings.source_hint: Contact Support form validation: steps 7-12, 31-42, 73-78, and the mobile flow leading to generic “Please fill all fields”

findings.user_goal: Understand that interactions are working while typing/searching
findings.problem: The agent’s detection reports “no obvious visible/text change” after some input actions, which may reflect subtle UI feedback gaps (or at least makes it unclear whether the user should expect immediate change).
findings.evidence: Typed text action: “Typed into the ‘Search GitHub’ input... however the tool feedback says no obvious visible/text change was detected.” In contrast, later screenshots confirm the query was present; submission behavior then changed results.
findings.why_it_matters: If similar behavior exists for real users (e.g., weak live feedback, unclear focus states), it can reduce confidence, particularly on mobile.
findings.suggestion: Ensure clear focus styles and immediate confirmation for typing (caret/focus ring, visible query text update, and accessible status announcements).
findings.source_hint: Search input typing: session_memory notable signals; steps around typing react and then clicking Search
